templates.descriptionOfService:
We use the Meta Conversion API to send data on the actions that you take on our websites, such as visits to our sites, interaction with our content and reservations made on our website (together referred to as “Event Data”) from your browser and our website through a server to Meta Ireland Limited (“Meta”). 

Meta will render measurement and analytics services for us and provide us with campaign reports that show the impressions on our websites, as well as generate analytics and insights about your use of our websites and services. This helps us optimize our ads, improve their efficiency and tailor our content to your interests and needs.  

Through the Conversion API, we can also match information that personally identifies you, such as names, email addresses and phone numbers (together referred to as “Contact Information”) with Meta. Your Contact Information will always be hashed prior to transmission. Contact Information is used solely to match against user IDs and combine those user IDs with corresponding Event Data. Meta will delete Contact Information following the matching process.  

When you give consent to using this technology, your browser automatically establishes a connection to Meta’s server via their integrated Meta pixel. The above mentioned Event Data and hashed Contact Data are transmitted directly to Meta via a server connection using the API.   

This technology enables us to create Custom Audiences, optimize ad targeting, improve result measurement, generate aggregated reports on our advertising campaigns and gain analytics and insights into people's use of our websites and services.  

Generally Meta processes your personal data as a data processor on behalf of Sixt pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR.  

For the processing of personal data in Event Data referring to your actions on our websites we and Meta are considered Joint Controllers. This means we both determine the purposes and means of processing the data and share responsibility for its protection. Accordingly, we have entered a Controller Addendum with Meta Ireland Limited, which can be accessed through https://www.facebook.com/legal/businesstech?_rdr. If you have any questions or wish to access the data processed through this service, please contact Meta Ireland Limited, who will handle your request.  

If you give your consent, to the use of Meta Conversion API, Meta may also transfer your personal data to their affiliated companies in third countries outside the EU/EEA, including Meta Platforms Inc. in the United States of America. The data protection laws in the third countries may not offer the same level of protection as offered under the GDPR. Meta Platforms, Inc. has certified its participation in the EU-US. Data Privacy Framework, and transfers of personal data from Meta to Meta Plaforms, Inc. are generally based on the European Commission's related adequacy decision. For more information on onward transfers from Meta, please refer to Meta’s European Data Transfer Addendum. 

You can find more information on the processing of your personal data by Meta in Meta data protection notices specified below.

disclosures.description: Hotjar cookie that is set once a visitor completes a survey using the On-site Survey widget. It is used to ensure that the same survey does not reappear if it has already been filled in.

disclosures.name: _hjMinimizedPolls
disclosures.description: Hotjar cookie that is set once a visitor minimizes an On-site Survey widget. It is used to ensure that the widget stays minimized when the visitor navigates through your site.

disclosures.name: _hjShownFeedbackMessage
disclosures.description: Hotjar cookie that is set when a visitor minimizes or completes Incoming Feedback. This is done so that the Incoming Feedback will load as minimized immediately if the visitor navigates to another page where it is set to show.

disclosures.name: _hjid
disclosures.description: Hotjar cookie that is set when the customer first lands on a page with the Hotjar script. It is used to persist the Hotjar User ID, unique to that site on the browser. This ensures that behavior in subsequent visits to the same site will be attributed to the same user ID.

disclosures.name: _hjTLDTest
disclosures.description: When the Hotjar script executes we try to determine the most generic cookie path we should use, instead of the page hostname. This is done so that cookies can be shared across subdomains (where applicable). To determine this, we try to store the _hjTLDTest cookie for different URL substring alternatives until it fails. After this check, the cookie is removed.

disclosures.name: _hjUserAttributesHash
disclosures.description: User Attributes sent through the Hotjar Identify API are cached for the duration of the session in order to know when an attribute has changed and needs to be updated.

disclosures.name: _hjCachedUserAttributes
disclosures.description: This cookie stores User Attributes which are sent through the Hotjar Identify API, whenever the user is not in the sample. These attributes will only be saved if the user interacts with a Hotjar Feedback tool.

disclosures.name: _hjLocalStorageTest
disclosures.description: This cookie is used to check if the Hotjar Tracking Script can use local storage. If it can, a value of 1 is set in this cookie. The data stored in_hjLocalStorageTest has no expiration time, but it is deleted almost immediately after it is created.

disclosures.name: _hjIncludedInPageviewSample
disclosures.description: This cookie is set to let Hotjar know whether that visitor is included in the data sampling defined by your site's pageview limit.

disclosures.name: _hjIncludedInSessionSample
disclosures.description: This cookie is set to let Hotjar know whether that visitor is included in the data sampling defined by your site's daily session limit.

disclosures.name: _hjAbsoluteSessionInProgress
disclosures.description: This cookie is used to detect the first pageview session of a user. This is a True/False flag set by the cookie.

disclosures.name: _hjFirstSeen
disclosures.description: This is set to identify a new user’s first session. It stores a true/false value, indicating whether this was the first time Hotjar saw this user. It is used by Recording filters to identify new user sessions.

disclosures.name: hjViewportId
disclosures.description: This is set to identify a new user’s first session. It stores a true/false value, indicating whether this was the first time Hotjar saw this user. It is used by Recording filters to identify new user sessions.

disclosures.name: _hjRecordingEnabled
disclosures.description: This is added when a Recording starts and is read when the recording module is initialized to see if the user is already in a recording in a particular session.

disclosures.name: _hjSessionUser {site_id}
disclosures.description: This cookie is set when a user first lands on a page with the Hotjar script. It is used to persist the Hotjar User ID, unique to that site on the browser. This ensures that behavior in subsequent visits to the same site will be attributed to the same user ID.

disclosures.name: _hjSession{site_id}
disclosures.description: This cookie holds the current session data. This ensures that subsequent requests within the session window will be attributed to the same Hotjar session.

disclosures.name: _hjSessionTooLarge
disclosures.description: This cookie causes Hotjar to stop collecting data if a session becomes too large. This is determined automatically by a signal from the WebSocket server if the session size exceeds the limit.

disclosures.name: _hjSessionRejected
disclosures.description: If present, this cookie will be set to '1' for the duration of a user's session, if Hotjar rejected the session from connecting to the WebSocket due to server overload. This cookie is only applied in extremely rare situations to prevent severe performance issues.

disclosures.name: _hjSessionResumed
disclosures.description: This cookie is set when a session/recording is reconnected to Hotjar servers after a break in connection.

templates.descriptionOfService:
We use Google Customer Match to securely share information about you, such as your email address, phone number, or postal address (collectively referred to as "Contact Information"), with Google Ireland Limited (“Google”). This allows us to show you personalised ads across Google platforms, including Search, YouTube, Gmail, and Display. 

When you provide consent to use this technology, your Contact Information is hashed (converted into a code that cannot be reversed or recognized) locally on our systems before it is transmitted to Google. This process ensures your data is protected and cannot be read or accessed by anyone during transmission. Google uses this hashed data to match it with its user accounts. If a match is found, Google adds the user to an audience list that allows us to show tailored ads. 

Your hashed Contact Information is used solely for this matching process and is not stored or used by Google for any other purpose. Google deletes any unmatched or processed data within 48 hours after the process is completed. 

By consenting to this service, your browser or device establishes a secure connection with Google’s servers to facilitate the above-mentioned data matching and delivery of personalised ads. This process helps us provide ads that are more relevant to your preferences while adhering to strict privacy and security standards.
